look_here_first: Start with the middle-sized fruit and leaflet count. Arizona walnut usually carries 9–15 broader leaflets and fruits about 2–3.5 cm across—larger than little walnut but far smaller than typical black walnut fruit.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Bandera County Lost Maples / Edwards Plateau documentation; Real County spring-fed fen and Roaring Springs documentation; Uvalde County wild-collection associate documentation from Frio River headwaters.

best_field_traits: nut 1.8–2.7 cm, deeply longitudinally grooved but relatively smooth between grooves
streams, rocky canyon sides, springs and mesic canyon woodland
morphology_keys.comparison_training: J. microcarpa has 17–25 much narrower leaflets and tiny fruit; J. nigra has 15–23 leaflets plus much larger 3.5–8 cm fruit and coarsely warty nut sculpture.

comparisons.key_distinctions: J. microcarpa has 17–25 much narrower leaflets and tiny fruit; J. nigra has 15–23 leaflets plus much larger 3.5–8 cm fruit and coarsely warty nut sculpture.

taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Flora of North America warns that central Texas intermediates occur among local walnut species; use multiple characters on atypical material.
